title: 1 Chronicles 12
paragraphs: ¹² ¹ These are the men who came to David at Ziklag while he was still banished from the presence of Saul son of Kish. They were among the warriors who helped him in battle. ² They were armed with bows and could shoot arrows or sling stones with either the right or the left hand; they were kinsmen of Saul from the tribe of Benjamin. ³ Their leader was Ahiezer, then Joash — both sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; also Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; Jehu the Anathothite; ⁴ Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty warrior among the Thirty, who led the Thirty; ⁵ Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite;

⁶ Elkanah, Jesiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam the Korahites; ⁷ and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor. ⁸ Some Gadites defected to David at his stronghold in the wilderness. They were brave warriors, trained for battle and skilled with shield and spear. Their faces were like the faces of lions, and they were as swift as gazelles across the hills. ⁹ Ezer was the first, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third, ¹⁰ Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,

¹¹ Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh, ¹² Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth, ¹³ Jeremiah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh. ¹⁴ These Gadites were army commanders; the least of them was a match for a hundred men, and the greatest was a match for a thousand.

¹⁶ Men from Benjamin and Judah came to David at the stronghold. ¹⁷ David went out to meet them and said, "If you have come to me in peace to help me, then my heart will be united with yours. But if you have come to betray me to my enemies when I have done no wrong, then may the God of our fathers see it and judge you." ¹⁸ Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the thirty, and he said, "We are yours, David — we are on your side, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to all who help you, for your God helps you." David welcomed them and made them leaders of his raiding bands. ¹⁹ Some men of Manasseh also defected to David when he came with the Philistines to fight against Saul — though they did not help the Philistines, because the Philistine lords, after deliberation, sent David away. They said, "He will defect back to his master Saul, and it will cost us our heads." ²⁰ As David returned to Ziklag, these men of Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zilthai — all commanders of units in Manasseh.

²¹ They helped David against the raiding bands, for they were all valiant warriors and became commanders in his army. ²² Day after day men kept coming to help David, until his force was as vast as the army of God. ²³ These are the numbers of the armed troops who came to David at Hebron to hand over Saul's kingdom to him, just as the LORD had said. ²⁴ The men of Judah who carried shield and spear: six thousand eight hundred armed and ready for battle. ²⁵ Of the men of Simeon, valiant warriors for war: seven thousand one hundred.

²⁶ Of the descendants of Levi: four thousand six hundred. ²⁷ Jehoiada was the leader of the Aaronites, and with him were three thousand seven hundred. ²⁸ Zadok, a young warrior of great ability, came with twenty-two commanders from his own family. ²⁹ Of the men of Benjamin, kinsmen of Saul: three thousand — for until then most of them had remained loyal to the house of Saul. ³⁰ Of the men of Ephraim: twenty thousand eight hundred valiant warriors, famous men throughout their clans.

³¹ Of the half-tribe of Manasseh: eighteen thousand, who were designated by name to come and make David king. ³² Of the men of Issachar, who had understanding of the times and knew what Israel should do: two hundred chiefs, with all their kinsmen under their command. ³³ Of Zebulun: fifty thousand seasoned troops equipped for battle with every weapon of war, all ready to fight with a single purpose of heart. ³⁴ Of Naphtali: one thousand commanders, with thirty-seven thousand men carrying shield and spear. ³⁵ Of the Danites, battle-ready troops: twenty-eight thousand six hundred.

³⁶ Of Asher: forty thousand experienced troops ready for battle. ³⁷ From the east side of the Jordan, men of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh: one hundred and twenty thousand equipped with every kind of weapon. ³⁸ All these warriors, lined up in battle formation, came to Hebron with a single heart to make David king over all Israel. And all the rest of Israel also shared this one purpose — to make David king. ³⁹ They spent three days there with David, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen had made provision for them. ⁴⁰ Moreover, their neighbors from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen — supplies of flour, figs, raisins, wine, olive oil, and oxen and sheep in abundance, for there was joy in Israel.
